ay9pkb:280: Traditional automated testing can only judge whether a feature works—an API returning 200 is success, a timeout is failure. But AI system outputs are often judged on dimensions that binary decisions cannot measure: content quality, expression fluency, strategy soundness. The author introduces the Rubrics concept: for content quality evaluation scenarios, generate a series of test cases graded at different levels (for example, in an OKR query scenario, "merely checking whether results were found is underwhelming—instead, you can generate a series of different quality levels"). This design solves the core challenge of AI evaluation: replacing subjective judgment with rule-based, structured evaluation sets. Each Rubrics dimension has clearly defined scoring criteria; the AI only needs to determine which level the current output maps to—more reliable and more explainable than directly outputting "whether the content is good."

The author's AI First philosophy completely inverts this contradiction—rather than having AI assist humans in evaluation, it makes human intervention impossible from the entry point, with all evaluation actions executed autonomously by AI.
